findings.reason: a worker implementing §22 has to invent both the source set the rebuild reads and which of the two eligibility procedures governs a rolled file, and the plausible single-source implementation silently retires nothing, defeating the section's whole purpose after §21 lands.
findings.text: §22 says the pass "rebuilds those tiers from the complete raw record with the existing full compaction" and stages each result "into a scratch path beside the tier file", but this node runs after §21 (node table, line 860), which renames a running serve's raw file into day segments `<slug>-<job>.<YYYYMMDD>.jsonl` (§21:839), so an ended job's "complete raw record" is a set of segments rather than one file; `telemetry_store.compact_file(source, destination)` takes a single source and writes its destination with `destination.write_text(...)` (telemetry_store.py:811–816), so compacting segment by segment into one tier path leaves that tier holding only the last segment's rows — it will never prove equal to the job's raw record, and every rolled job stays permanently ineligible; the same paragraph also conflicts with §21:841, which makes a closed day segment "eligible for the existing retirement check on the same terms as a file whose job has ended" and pairs that segment with the ladder's windows inside its UTC day, whereas §22 makes eligibility turn on a whole-record rebuild that for a still-running job does not exist and whose `os.replace` would replace a live ladder the recorder is still appending to

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `node_probe.py:186`, `:667`, `telemetry_store.compact_file`, the `s22-1278105` anchor and the `scheduled-retirement` decision all resolve; the extensionless snapshot hrefs resolve as `<path>.html`.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §22's done-when names measurable assertions and a declared negative control ("skips the digest re-check, and a file mutated between listing and apply must be caught"), plus the keep-path control "a file whose rebuilt tiers still disagree is kept".
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the section's evidence is a durable repository path (`docs/evidence/archive/serving-record-warehouse-landed.html#s22-1278105`); nothing in §22 writes to a scratchpad or a node-local temporary directory.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §22's mechanism names carry no plan labels, stage names or ticket numbers.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §22's changed rebuild paragraph does not say which files the rebuild reads now that §21 has split a job's raw record into day segments, and the single-source `compact_file` it invokes overwrites its destination, so the mechanism cannot produce the equality its own done-when asserts.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — the node's parts (scheduled apply, rebuild-before-compare, bounded liveness read, index vacuum) are one deliverable: retention runs on a schedule and the index gives the space back.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — the `srw-scheduled-retention` node's "runs after §21" names a node that exists, the `scheduled-retirement` decision carries `data-sections="s22"`, and the §5 ingest loop it attaches to exists (`telemetry_ingest.py:64`, `DEFAULT_CADENCE_SECONDS = 60.0`).
